subject: Questions about copy command and multivariate models

messages.author: cc27dfd4a9d94026
messages.subject: Questions about copy command and multivariate models
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to transition from MCMC to INLA but am having trouble understanding the details of language. I was wondering if someone who has been using INLA for a while could offer some guidance.

I believe I need to use the copy feature to write the model I need, but I can not entirely follow how this feature works. Essentially, I have two Poisson outcomes with common covariates and correlated random effects from a bivariate Gaussian. But I keep getting stuck.

I've seen this example:

n = 100
Sigma = matrix(c(1, 0.8, 0.8, 1), 2, 2)
x = rnorm(n)
ab = rmvnorm(n, sigma = Sigma)
a = ab[, 1]
b = ab[, 2]
eta = a + b * x
y = eta + rnorm(n, sd = 1)

hyper.gaussian = list(prec = list(prior="loggamma", param=c(1,0.2161)))
i = 1:n
j = 1:n + n
formula = y ~ f(i, model="iid2d", n=2*n) + f(j, x, copy="i") - 1
result = inla(formula, data = list(y = y, x = x, i = i, j = j), family = "gaussian", control.predictor=list(link=1),control.family = list(hyper = hyper.gaussian))



Which I can also convert to JAGS:


modelJAGS = function() {  
  for(i in 1:n) {
    y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i],tau)
    mu[i] <- AB[i,1] + AB[i,2]*x[i]
  }
 
  for(i in 1:n){
    AB[i,1:2] ~ dmnorm(mu.W[], tau.W[ ,])
   
  }
 
  tau ~ dgamma(0.01,0.01)
  tau.W[1:2,1:2] ~ dwish(R[1:2,1:2],2)  
}  

mu.W = c(0,0)
R = structure(.Data = c(1, 0.8, 0.8, 1), .Dim = c(2, 2))


data = list("x","y","n","mu.W","R")
params = c("tau.W","tau","mu")

mod = jags(data=data,param=params,n.chains=2,n.iter=5000,n.burnin=2000,model.file=modelJAGS) ; mod



And I get nearly identical predicted values. But I can't make the leap to say transferring this to INLA:



modelJAGS = function() {  
  for(i in 1:n) {
    y1[i] ~ dpois(mu1[i])
    y2[i] ~ dpois(mu2[i])
    log(mu1[i]) <- alpha1 + NU[i,1]
    log(mu2[i]) <- alpha1 + NU[i,2]
  }
 
  for(i in 1:n) {
    NU[i,1:2] ~ dmnorm(mu.NU[], tau.NU[ ,])
  }
 
  alpha1  ~ dnorm(0,0.001)
  tau.NU[1:2,1:2] ~ dwish(R[1:2,1:2],2)
 
}  

mu.NU = c(0,0)
R = structure(.Data = c(0.1, 0, 0, 0.1), .Dim = c(2, 2))

data$mu.NU = mu.NU
data$R = R
data$x = x
data$y1 = y1
data$y2 = y2
data$n = n
data = list("y1","y2","n","mu.NU","R")
params = c("tau.NU","mu1","mu2","alpha1")

mod = jags(data=data,param=params,n.chains=2,n.iter=5000,n.burnin=2000,model.file=modelJAGS)  


I've tried, but I don't get close predicted values and I think my INLA code is incorrect:

m = length(y1)
Y = cbind( c(y1, rep(NA,m)), c( rep(NA,m), y2) ) ; Y  
z1 = c( 1:m, rep(NA,m)) ; z1  
z2 = c( rep(NA,m), 1:m) ; z2


formula = Y ~ f(z1, model="iid2d",n=2*m) + f(z2, copy="z1")
data = data.frame(Y=Y,z1=z1,z2=z2) ; data
m = inla(formula,data=data,family=rep("poisson",2),control.predictor=list(link=1))  

I don't understand why there is a  "-1" at the end of the formula in the first example, and adding this does not fix the problem in the second example. Apologies for dumb questions and thanks very much for any help!

-K

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Questions about copy command and multivariate models
parts:
Hi,

you have to use something like
formula = Y ~ 0 + i1 + i2 + f(z1, model="iid2d",n=2*m)
data = list(Y=Y, z1 = 1:(2*m),
i1=rep(0:1,each=m), i2=rep(1:0,each=m))
where
i1 and i2 are used to fit the intercepts
z1 to the 2xm effects

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Questions about copy command and multivariate models
parts:
Thanks so much, that's super helpful. So I don't even need the copy command there, I think I understand. 

Now I'm trying to make the leap to a bivariate time-series model that I've implemented in JAGS. So using simple simulated data like:
n = 100
set.seed(1453)  
x = arima.sim(model=list(ar=c(0.5)),n=n) + 10
y1 = rpois(n,x) + 5
y2 = rpois(n,x) + 2
Tn = length(x)


And JAGS code something like:


 model = function() {
   for(t in 1:Tn) {
     y1[t] ~ dpois(mu1[t])
     y2[t] ~ dpois(mu2[t])
     log(mu1[t]) <- alpha1 + beta1*x[t] + b1[t]
     log(mu2[t]) <- alpha2 + beta2*x[t] + b2[t]
   }
 
   for(t in 2:Tn){
     b1[t] <- rho1*b1[t-1] + W[t,1]
     b2[t] <- rho2*b2[t-1] + W[t,2]
     W[t,1:2] ~ dmnorm(mu.W[], tau.W[ ,])
   }



Etc. 

This is where I get really stuck with INLA - how to have both an ar1 process and the correlated error on the ar1 between the two outcomes. I think I might have something almost correct, but the predicted values are not quite the same (could be priors, or I've done something wrong):

 m = length(y1)
 Y = cbind(c(y1, rep(NA,m)), c(rep(NA,m), y2)) ; head(Y)
 
 i1 = rep(0:1, each=m) ; i1
 i2 = rep(1:0,each=m) ; i2
 z1 = c( 1:m, rep(NA,m)) ; z1
 z2 = c( rep(NA,m), 1:m) ; z2
 z3 = z1
 xx = c(x, rep(NA,m))
 
 formula = Y ~ xx + i1 + i2  + f(z1, model="ar1")  + f(z2, copy="z1") + f(z3, model="iid2d",n=2*m)  
 
 data = data.frame(Y=Y,xx=xx,z1=z1,z2=z2,z3=z3,i1=i1,i2=i2) ; head(data) ; tail(data)
 
 m = inla(formula,data=data,family=rep("poisson",2),control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE))  


Thanks again!

parts: Yes, now the copy is the way. Because you have a multivariate (bivariate) effect at each time you may follow the example for the spatio temporal model ('iid2d' instead 'generic1') in http://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/r-inla.org/papers/DLM_examples_2011-10-23.R

Thanks so much, that's super helpful. So I don't even need the copy command there, I think I understand. 

Now I'm trying to make the leap to a bivariate time-series model that I've implemented in JAGS. So using simple simulated data like:

set.seed(1453)  
x = arima.sim(model=list(ar=c(0.5)),n=n) + 10
y1 = rpois(n,x) + 5
y2 = rpois(n,x) + 2
Tn = length(x)

     log(mu2[t]) <- alpha2 + beta2*x[t] + b2[t]
   }

     b2[t] <- rho2*b2[t-1] + W[t,2]
     W[t,1:2] ~ dmnorm(mu.W[], tau.W[ ,])

Etc. 

This is where I get really stuck with INLA - how to have both an ar1 process and the correlated error on the ar1 between the two outcomes. I think I might have something almost correct, but the predicted values are not quite the same (could be priors, or I've done something wrong):
